tagline.text: Eastern Visayas' highest summit, a mossy-forest peak in Leyte

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱355–1,000 (day hike; excludes travel to Ormoc)

children.text: Alto Peak rises in Ormoc City on Leyte Island at about 1,332 m and is known as the highest mountain in Eastern Visayas. You climb with a local guide from Barangay Cabintan, passing steep rope sections and root-clambering slopes to reach a summit often wrapped in cloud.
Alto Peak sits in the interior of Ormoc City on the western side of Leyte Island. Sources differ slightly on its height: the Ormoc City tourism description and climbing websites give about
, while Wikipedia's list of regional high points gives about

. Either way, it is the highest point in Eastern Visayas (Region VIII). Locals also call it Mt. Aminduen, and "alto" means "high" in Spanish. It is sometimes counted among the Seven Summits of the Philippines.
There are two main ways up. One starts from Barangay Cabintan, close to Ormoc city proper; one trip report says it took about
2.5 hours
from the jump-off to the summit. The other is a long, remote route from Lake Danao via Lake Janagdan; climbing sites list about
12.5 hours
to the summit and suggest 3 days and 2 nights or 4 days and 3 nights. Most travelers take the Cabintan route and either hike it as a day trip or camp one night.

Higher up, the forest is covered in moss and roots, clouds are frequent, and fixed ropes hang on the steepest sections. One trip report describes a midway section that felt close to 80 degrees and recommends using a rope. The summit is said to be a grassy patch about
wide with cliffs on both sides, and when the clouds part you can see western Leyte and, far off, Biliran Island.

This is not a developed tourist mountain. There are no stalls, only Smart is said to have a stable mobile signal, and the trail is maintained only at the level of a local guide association. That also means few crowds and a rugged charm, making it an unusual day out in Leyte for travelers with the fitness and preparation. If you have little hiking experience, you can skip the summit and explore Ormoc city and the Lake Danao area instead. Climbing sites rate Alto Peak 6/9 in difficulty, so judge your fitness, the weather and guide availability and do not push beyond your limits.

blocks.title: Summit of Eastern Visayas' Highest Peak

children.text: The summit is said to have a small grassy area and a few small trees. Reports say you can shelter beside the trees when the wind turns cold. In clear weather, views open over western Leyte toward Ormoc.

Beyond the midpoint, the trail runs through forest of moss-covered trees, rocks and small waterfalls. Trip reports also mention wild strawberries and garden-like scenery. Many sections involve pulling yourself up slippery roots by hand, so gloves help.
One section midway is very steep and uses fixed ropes. A trip report says it felt like about 70–90 degrees. The tip is to climb with your legs and not hang from the rope.
This remote lake is described as sitting in a crater. On the long Cabintan route, one record says it was reached in about
2 hours
. Day hikes often skip it.
Reports say you can spend a night near the summit or at the camp. Some trip reports mention a water source and a small waterfall nearby. On clear nights, many stars are said to be visible.
A campsite near the trail's exit, listed at about
per night, with showers at about

Register at the barangay office (about

Start from the trailhead and climb through forest. Slopes and root sections follow one another, and on steep parts the guide explains how to use the ropes.
According to trip reports, it takes about
2–3 hours
to reach the grassy summit. Enjoy the view and have lunch, though the wind is cold and it is hard to stay long.
Descend by the same route. Wet roots and muddy paths are slippery, so going down takes more care.
Return to Cabintan, settle the guide fee and head back to Ormoc.
Round-trip times vary widely with weather and fitness, so start early and begin your descent by the afternoon at the latest.
Attend the briefing at Cabintan, register and set off. The 2018 trip report started in mid-morning.
Reach Lake Janagdan, rest and have lunch.
Follow the forest trail to a junction, then walk about
1 hour
more to reach camp and pitch your tent.
Wake early the next day, have breakfast and set out for the summit. Leave large bags at camp and climb light.
Come down from the summit, have lunch at camp, then descend toward Heaven's Peak.
This itinerary is based on a 2018 trip report and the trail may have changed, so agree on the plan with your guide first. Guides may also store spare gear at camp.
The usual way is to fly from Manila (NAIA) to Tacloban (TAC). Trip reports say the flight takes at least about
1 hour 20 minutes
. Check the latest timetables.
From Tacloban airport, go to the bus terminal, then take a bus or van to Ormoc, which is said to take about
3 hours

There is also a route that skips the direct Ormoc boat: travel to Hilongos or Baybay port, then take a bus or van to Ormoc, which takes about
1.5–2.5 hours
. Check shipping line notices for schedules and fares.
One report says you can take a jeepney or multicab from Ormoc terminal toward Lake Danao and get off at the Cabintan entrance in about
20 minutes
for about

If you have a rental car, searching for Alto Peak in a map app reportedly gives about

According to climbing websites, the driest months are February to May. April has the fewest rainy days (about 6), while July and October have the most (about 19). Summit temperatures are said to stay around
by day and
at night all year.

Rain makes the rope sections and root climbs very slippery and is said to bring out more leeches, so climb on a dry-season weekday if you can. One trip report describes heavy rain while camping in June.

It is easiest to stay in Ormoc city before and after the hike. Ormoc is a large city in western Leyte with plenty of hotels and restaurants, and Cabintan is only about
20 minutes
from the center. Near Cabintan, the Heaven's Peak campsite lets you pitch a tent for about
a night, and showers are said to cost about

Nothing sells food or water on the mountain. Trip reports advise bringing at least about 3 liters of water, trail food, electrolyte drinks, and a tent and cooking set if you will camp. If you bring food to eat in the village, there is said to be a table fee of about
for a large table and about
for a small one. Plan to eat at restaurants in Ormoc city.

Ormoc city has large restaurants and convenience stores, which makes it a good place to buy snacks and water the day before your hike. After the descent, many travelers warm up with a hot soup in town. Room rates vary by season, so check booking sites for current prices.
Always register at Cabintan before you climb and go with a local guide. Reports say the trail is undeveloped and the route near the summit is not clearly marked.
Bring at least about 3 liters of water, and leave large bags in the village or at camp so you climb light.
Wear trekking shoes with good grip and bring long gloves, leggings and arm guards. Roots and thorny plants are said to scratch easily.
On rope sections, climbing with your legs rather than your arms is said to keep your body from swinging side to side.
One source says visitors are received until
, so start day hikes in the morning.
Trip reports say Smart has the most stable signal, so prepare a SIM for contact in advance.
If you are new to hiking, build fitness on smaller mountains first. Trip reports also recommend practice climbs.
Follow Leave No Trace and carry all of your trash out.
The wind at the summit is cold, so pack a windproof jacket and spare socks in a waterproof bag. You chill quickly once the sweat cools.
When you reach Cabintan, ask about guide fees and the plan first, and for larger groups agree on the number of guides and how payment is split. One report describes one guide covering up to 5 people.

The route near the summit is unclear, very steep and has cliffs, so do not climb without a guide. Before you leave, check with the Ormoc City tourism office or Cabintan barangay whether the mountain is open and what the current fees are.
The summit is a grassy patch about
wide with cliffs on both sides, so stay away from the edges.
Roots and rocks become very slippery in the rain. Trip reports mention leeches, thorny plants and stinging insects.
Cloud, rain and cold wind are frequent near the summit, so bring light windproof and waterproof clothing.
One source mentions places with a sulfur smell on the route from Lake Janagdan to camp. Follow your guide's instructions near geothermal areas.
Fees, reception hours and contacts differ between reports and may change. Check the latest notices before you go.
A lake in the hills above Ormoc known for its guitar shape; there is also a long route to Alto Peak that starts from Lake Danao. It is said to take about
45 minutes
from the city.
